body:
Third step of the simulation-thread / immutable-Scene renderer revamp (after #522 and #534). **Interactive games now run the simulation on its own thread while the main thread handles input, GUI logic and drawing.** Drawing reads only the extracted `Scene`. This is the default with no setting. The browser build and hosts where thread creation fails step the same session serially, which also remains the headless default and the equivalence reference. No simulation, save, replay or network format change.

Evidence branch: [`evidence/threaded-renderer-sim-thread`](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/tree/evidence/threaded-renderer-sim-thread) (pixel captures, checksum sidecars and hashes, ThreadSanitizer logs, benchmark script and results; see its README).

## Changes (one commit each)
1. **Extract the frame's Scene once per frame** through `extractScene`.
2. **Units, buildings, effects, particles, the minimap and overlays draw from the Scene.** `SceneEntities` holds per-unit and per-building draw data indexed by gid, plus the selection's map contribution. The overlay map refreshes per 25-tick window inside `SceneExtractor`.
3. **Selection panels, the HUD and statistics draw from the Scene** (`ScenePanels`, which includes a copy of the local team's stats). Touch actions re-validate against the live building before issuing orders.
4. **Building placement previews draw from the Scene** (`SceneMap::isHardSpaceForBuilding`).
5. **The torus view's selection markers draw from the Scene.**
6. **`VoiceRecorder` thread flags are atomic.** This was a pre-existing race that ThreadSanitizer reported.
7. **Run the simulation on its own thread** (`src/sim/SimulationRunner`):
   - The simulation thread paces itself on the host clock, which excludes time in the background. It runs `Engine::simulationStep`, then extracts a Scene into the triple buffer only once the main thread has taken the previous one.
   - Input, `GameGUI::step`, client events, selection checks and script highlights run in `withGame`, with the simulation parked between ticks.
   - Values the client sets and extraction reads go through the locked `ClientRequests`. This now includes the drawn map size, which TSan caught being shared through `Map`.
   - Pause, hard pause, running state and CPU load are atomics. Pause and local-quit orders still take effect in the same tick.
   - Failures on the simulation thread are rethrown on the main thread into the existing abort path. Suspending the app parks the simulation.
   - `GLOB2_SIM_THREAD=1` runs headless sessions threaded, for equivalence checks. `GLOB2_SIM_THREAD=0` forces serial, for exact frame-count tests.
8. **Threaded drawing is capped by frame time instead of a fixed 8 ms wait.** The fixed wait stacked on top of vsync and held drawing near 45 fps.

## Verification (macOS, Apple M3, Apple clang 21)
- **Simulation equivalence:** `check_sim_thread.py` compares the branch against a master baseline over five scenarios: two new 4-AI games, a generated map, a v121 legacy save, and save continuation. Checksum sidecars, replay bytes and final saves are identical both threaded (`--candidate-env GLOB2_SIM_THREAD=1`) and serial. Re-run after rebasing onto #534 and #535.
- **`EngineSession`:** runs a full `GameSessionScreen` game on the simulation thread, including suspension. Its checksum equals the three serial sessions.
- **Pixel parity against master:** 30 `SoftwareRenderBenchmark` captures from 30k- and 15k-tick saves:
  - map and GUI modes at three zooms;
  - selected building, flag and unit;
  - the inn placement tool.

  29 are byte-identical. The remaining one differs only in a 16×13 region that also changes between two master runs.
- **ThreadSanitizer:** windowed 4-AI `-test-games` (300 and 400 ticks) and headless threaded `--run-game` (600 ticks). The two races found (drawn map size; `VoiceRecorder`) are fixed here. No other reports.
- **Tests:** `run_tests.py`: 306 passed. The 8 failures are all local-environment ones that are unrelated to this PR:
  - `Settings` layout ×6 (fullscreen switching);
  - `MapPreview` fade timing;
  - the unit binary's dummy-driver window creation in `OpaqueRectangleBatch`, a known master failure.

  Targeted `EngineSession`, `TorusRender`, `GameGUI*`, `Scene*`, `SharedWorker*`, `ComputeExecutor*` and `ClientChannels*` re-run after the rebase: all pass.
- **Not verified locally:** Linux, Windows, Android, iOS and browser are left to CI. The browser path is serial and unchanged. Known master CI failures are listed in #534.

## Performance (windowed, 1024×768 software renderer, balanced map, 4 AIs, seed 5)

| Preset, ticks | Cores | Serial: wall, fps | Threaded: wall, fps |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8 (3 ms ticks), 3000 | performance | 9.0 s, 67 fps | 9.0 s, **115 fps** |
| 8, 12000 | performance | 36.4 s, 66 fps | 36.0 s, **96 fps** |
| 10 (uncapped), 3000 | performance | 2.24 s, 84 fps | **0.70 s**, 108 fps |
| 10, 12000 | performance | 12.1 s, 62 fps | **9.3 s**, 82 fps |
| 8, 3000 (×3) | efficiency (`taskpolicy -c background`) | 33.5–35.2 s (far behind pace), 17–18 fps | **9.05 s (on pace)**, 18–19 fps |
| 10, 3000 (×3) | efficiency | 13.1–13.9 s, 14 fps | **3.5–4.0 s**, 17–18 fps |

At fast presets, serial draws only every 5th tick (preset 8) or every 16th (preset 10). Threaded draws every display frame and keeps the simulation on pace. On the efficiency cores (four throttled cores, a rough stand-in for a weak phone), threaded holds pace at preset 8, where serial falls almost 4× behind, and runs the uncapped preset 3.5× faster. Timings there vary strongly with machine load. An earlier single run showed threaded slower at the uncapped preset; it did not reproduce in three alternating repeats (`efficiency-repeats.txt` on the evidence branch). Real low-end Android measurement is still pending.

## Feel
- Fast-forward looks smoother: the screen updates every display frame (about 100 fps) instead of every 5th or 16th tick. Units still move per tick, so higher frame rates repeat tick states until the optional interpolation setting lands.
- At the uncapped preset, the game itself runs faster in real time (1.3–3.5× above), because drawing no longer takes simulation time.
- Input is applied at the next tick boundary, the same tick as in serial play.
- Please play-test on a phone, especially fast-forward late in a game.

## Follow-ups
- Optional unit interpolation graphics setting (default off; byte-identical when off).
- Measure on a real low-end Android device. If the CPU is saturated there, consider keeping one core for drawing when threaded (the default AI worker count equals the number of AI players, up to 4).
- Per-thread telemetry: the simulation thread's perf scopes are recorded in its own thread-local collector and not yet reported.
- Browser threading is now possible after #535. The browser currently stays serial, as decided.
- Include-boundary test for `src/render`/`src/gui`, and a TSan CI job.
